ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a pair of similar triangles. Beside the smaller blue triangle on the left, the corresponding side length is labeled 10 mm, and the area is labeled A = 25 mm². Beside the larger green triangle on the right, the corresponding side length is labeled 18 mm. Reasoning: The linear scale factor of similar figures is 18/10 = 1.8. The area scale factor equals the square of the linear scale factor, so the area of the green figure = 25 × (18/10)^2 = 25 × 3.24 = 81. Therefore the area of the green figure is 81.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as showing two similar triangular figures: the smaller blue triangle has a corresponding side labeled 10 mm and area labeled A = 25 mm², while the larger green triangle has the corresponding side labeled 18 mm. Use the linear scale factor from blue to green, 18/10 = 1.8. Since the figures are similar, the area scale factor is the square of the linear scale factor, so multiply the blue area by (1.8)^2: 25 × (18/10)^2 = 25 × 3.24 = 81. Therefore the green area is 81.
